name: bolognese
instructions:
TWO BOLOGNESE VARIANTS. Both share: tomato base + a protein + wine + soffrito-style aromatics + long simmer intent + pasta. Variant A is the canonical bolognese (Marcella); VARIANT B IS MY BOLOGNESE — the core recipe of this file, rebuilt around the meat-thing-minimum rule (see below). (Nisha's and ATK's vegetarian recipes are kept as CONTEXT in the notes.)

LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS ARE SECONDARY/OK in this recipe (see notes — the allowance does NOT extend to [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]]). The protein slot is a meat thing, real or fake — but IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF IS BANNED (clashing — it ages horribly; see notes). ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA BOLOGNESE (CANONICAL) ===

The load-bearing recipe in this family. Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking. If 'bolognese' means one thing in this cookbook, it's this one.

INGREDIENTS:
- vegetable oil + butter (the fat)
- yellow onions, celery, carrots — finely diced soffrito
- ground beef (or abbots ground beef as the substitute)
- milk
- nutmeg
- WHITE wine (Marcella's canonical; red wine also appears in some bolognese traditions — see WINE note)
- canned tomatoes
- black pepper
- pasta (traditionally tagliatelle, not spaghetti)
- parmesan cheese for serving

TECHNIQUE — MARCELLA'S NON-NEGOTIABLES:
1. Cook the beef ONLY until it loses raw color. Do NOT brown it. Browning gives a different (and lesser) ragu.
2. Milk goes in BEFORE wine. The milk coats the meat and protects it from the wine acid; reversing the order changes the texture.
3. Bare-simmer for THREE+ HOURS uncovered. Splash in water if it dries out. The long uncovered simmer is what makes it a bolognese; cutting time turns it into a generic meat sauce.
4. Fat should separate at the end. That's the visual signal you're done.

=== VARIANT B — MY BOLOGNESE (THE CORE RECIPE) ===

Mine. The current build:

- SOFFRITO: celery / onion, in OLIVE OIL + BUTTER. NO CARROTS — too sweet (see notes).
- GARLIC.
- PROTEIN — THE MEAT-THING-MINIMUM RULE: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM — ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best. It's like a french beef stew — you need a meat thing even if it's fake. (Real ground beef obviously qualifies.) IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF IS BANNED — gummy, candy-like, artificial the day after (see notes).
- MILK + NUTMEG (watch the nutmeg — it can embitter; see the bitterness note).
- WINE DEGLAZE.
- SAUCE: CANNED TOMATO SAUCE — not tomato paste, not crushed tomatoes (this is where I think Nisha is wrong). HALF A CAN is generally enough, with ENOUGH MILK THAT IT'S CREAMY.
- HERBS: THYME + OREGANO are primary. ROSEMARY goes well here when there's ACTUAL MEAT in it.
- TOASTED WALNUTS: secondary option — toast first, don't overdo it (walnuts can embitter).
- IF VEGETARIAN: the recipe benefits from PORCINI POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST — and A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference (pub-lentils rules).
- DARK BALSAMIC VINEGAR — Nisha's discovery; the dish is incomplete without it. STAYS.
- CHEESE at the end: GRUYERE (funky — preferred) or parmesan.
- Serve with a PASTA WATER EMULSION.
notes:
THE BOLOGNESE SHAPE — WHAT BOTH VARIANTS HAVE IN COMMON:
1. A tomato base (canned tomatoes + often tomato paste; regular canned only — no fire-roasted; that's spaghetti-and-meatballs.json).
2. A protein slot: a MEAT THING — real ground beef (A) or vegan beef at bare minimum (B; ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best — impossible/beyond is banned). Lentils and mushrooms are secondary/OK (see below).
3. An acid: wine (white in A per Marcella's canonical; red per Nisha) + balsamic finish in B. See WINE note.
4. Soffrito-style FINELY DICED aromatics: yellow onion always in; celery/garlic; carrots in A only.
5. Long simmer intent (3+ hours for A; shorter for B).
6. Dairy: milk in both.
7. Served over pasta.

=== WINE — WHITE AND RED BOTH APPEAR ===

Both white and red wine appear frequently across canonical bolognese recipes:
- VARIANT A (Marcella): WHITE wine, canonically. Milk goes in first as a protective coat; white wine follows.
- VARIANT B: RED wine per Nisha's tradition; either works.
- CROSS-USE: either wine can work in either variant if that's what you have. Sticking to canonical is safer, but the family absorbs either.

Both wines are primary ingredients in this file for that reason.

=== THE MEAT-THING-MINIMUM RULE — VEGAN BEEF IS THE FLOOR; ABBOTS IS BEST; IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND IS BANNED ===

Core rule: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM for this recipe. It's like a FRENCH BEEF STEW — you need a meat thing, even if it's fake. The old vegetarian protein path (lentils + walnuts) no longer defines the core recipe. ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake-meat pick — same verdict as [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF — BANISHED AGAIN (CLASHING): it tastes good for 30 MINUTES after you make it, but it tastes HORRIBLE THE DAY AFTER — it becomes a GUMMY, CANDY-LIKE thing: not even sweet, just VERY ARTIFICIAL tasting. REMOVING CARROTS ISN'T ENOUGH. (This reverses the earlier reprieve — the carrots-out + balsamic/milk logic addressed the too-sweet problem, but the day-after aging failure is its own thing and it's disqualifying.)

=== CARROTS ARE OUT OF THE CORE RECIPE — TOO SWEET ===

Carrots are out of variant B: TOO SWEET. The soffrito is celery + onion. Carrots remain in variant A only, where Marcella's canonical soffrito keeps them.

=== LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS — SECONDARY/OK ===

Lentils, mushrooms, and walnuts are SECONDARY — OK in this recipe (walked forward from 'out entirely but orthogonal'). The allowance is bolognese-specific: they are NOT OK in [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

IF YOU WANT A MUSHROOM-FORWARD PASTA: see [[boscaiola]] (rich, cream + tomato paste + brandy + mushrooms; pasta al funghi, the lean expression, was deleted 2026-11-06). Lentil ragu history lives in the CONTEXT notes below.

=== HERBS — THE NO-HERB RULE IS OVERTURNED FOR THE CORE RECIPE ===

THYME + OREGANO are PRIMARY in variant B now (both were previously marked clashing — reversed). ROSEMARY goes well here WHEN THERE'S ACTUAL MEAT in it.

Variant A stays herb-free per Marcella — the long simmer + milk-and-nutmeg register is its own thing, and fresh herb finishes don't take.

Parsley stays clashing: a porcini powder/mushroom/parsley braise (Marcella — now [[marcella-mushrooms]]) would be good AS A SIDE to this — parsley doesn't need integration into the sauce itself.

=== PORCINI + NOOCH IF VEGETARIAN ===

When made vegetarian (abbots/vegan beef), the recipe benefits from PORCINI MUSHROOM POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST — glutamate support for what the real meat would otherwise bring. Following [[pub-style-lentils]] rules (porcini powder adds glutamates without tipping the scales), A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference here. (Whole mushrooms are secondary now — see the lentils/mushrooms/walnuts note.)

=== VARIANT B NOTES ===

WHERE NISHA IS WRONG, AND WHERE SHE'S RIGHT: her tomato-paste-forward sauce is the miss — this dish wants CANNED TOMATO SAUCE (half a can) with enough milk to read CREAMY, not a paste-dark reduction. But she knocks it out of the park with the BALSAMIC VINEGAR — the dish is incomplete without it. MILK AND BALSAMIC BOTH STAY — confirmed on the latest rework.

MILK, NOT CREAM: heavy cream would be clashing here — MILK is the most appropriate dairy. (Marcella's call stands across both variants: milk's lighter body protects and loosens without tipping the sauce into a cream-sauce register.)

BITTERNESS WATCH — WALNUTS AND NUTMEG: both can embitter. Toasted-but-not-overdone walnuts (secondary now), and a measured hand on the nutmeg.

CHEESE IN THE POT: funky GRUYERE preferred over parmesan, melted in at the end (matches the grating preference for variant A).

=== DISTINCTION FROM FIRE-ROASTED-MEATBALLS ===

Split off from this file. That dish uses fire-roasted tomatoes (load-bearing) and the meatball shape (load-bearing). Neither belongs in bolognese-shape.

=== DISTINCTION FROM LENTIL-MUSHROOM-STEW ===

That dish is a stew, not a ragu — broth-forward, served as a soup, explicitly anti-canned-tomato and anti-tomato-paste, uses stock not pasta. The lentils that used to live in this file's vegetarian variant point there and to [[sherry-french-lentils]] now.

=== WHY BOLOGNESE GETS THE HEADLINE ===

Variant A is the canonical italian ragu — Marcella Hazan's recipe is the cookbook's reference point. The three non-negotiables (don't brown the beef, milk before wine, three-hour uncovered simmer) define what 'bolognese' means here. Variant B borrows the bolognese shape as my own core recipe — it respects the shape without trying to be a copy of Marcella.

NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES IN THIS FILE: regular canned tomatoes only. Fire-roasted is the signature of spaghetti-and-meatballs.json.

TAGLIATELLE OVER SPAGHETTI FOR VARIANT A: Marcella was explicit that bolognese is for tagliatelle, not spaghetti. The wide flat noodle holds the meat sauce; spaghetti slides under it. Variant B is more forgiving — long-cut still preferred but ridged tubes (rigatoni, penne rigate) work fine.

GRUYERE OVER PARMESAN FOR GRATING ON TOP — MY PREFERENCE: I prefer grated gruyere over grated parmesan as the finishing cheese. The funkiness agrees with the sauce.

=== CONTEXT — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE (REFERENCE) ===

Nisha Vora, Rainbow Plant Life — the recipe the old vegetarian variant grew out of. Her build: onions browned with water-deglazing, garlic + oregano + thyme, a whole TUBE of tomato paste caramelized dark, red wine deglaze, 3 cups vegetable broth, 1 cup soaked RED lentils + 1/4 cup toasted crushed walnuts, canned crushed tomatoes, ~35-40 min simmer, 1 tbsp aged balsamic finish, parsley garnish. Her load-bearing claims, kept for reference: TUBE tomato paste over canned (canned reads tinny); soak the red lentils 30-60 min; TOAST the walnuts (raw walnut doesn't deliver — same as the retired lentil wellington's lesson); quality balsamic or skip (cheap balsamic is watery sourness); a commenter found it acidic without dairy — which the milk-and-tomato-sauce rework addresses directly.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — THE LENTIL/WALNUT AND MUSHROOM VARIANTS REMOVED ===

This file has walked through: four variants (Marcella; my mix; ATK mushroom; mushroom+lentil), then two (Marcella; lentil+walnut vegetarian), now two again with the vegetarian protein path replaced by the meat-thing-minimum rule. Mushrooms read stew; lentils now read as their own dish family. Both were orthogonal to bolognese for a while, then walked forward to secondary/OK (2026-11-04) — the same pass that banished impossible/beyond for its day-after aging failure.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[boscaiola]]: the mushroom-forward pasta home in this cookbook (pasta al funghi, the lean sibling, was deleted). Different shape (not bolognese).
- spaghetti-and-meatballs.json: fire-roasted tomatoes + meatball shape. Different shape.
- tomato pasta sauce family — [[marcella-gnocchi-sauce]] and [[pasta-piperade]] (the survivors): the protein-free italian pasta-sauce side. This bolognese file is the protein-forward, long-simmered counterpart.
